---
title: "Multiple users on Omarchy"
status: wip
---

Omarchy 4.0.x is still designed primarily as a single-user system. Creating another Linux account is straightforward, but that does **not** make the second account a fully configured Omarchy user.

Last checked on 2026-09-05.

::: {.callout-note}
Upstream discussion says native multi-user support is planned for Omarchy 4.1. Re-check this note after upgrading; much of it may become unnecessary.
:::

## create a non-admin account

For a family/guest account that should not have administrative privileges:

```bash
sudo useradd -m -s /bin/bash <user_name>
sudo passwd <user_name>
```

Do not add the account to `wheel` unless it should have administrative access.

The old version of this note also added the user to the `network` group. That is unnecessary on current Arch Linux: the `network` group is unused by default.

## Omarchy 4.0.x limitations

A second account will not automatically receive the first user's Omarchy configuration under `~/.config` and related per-user directories.

Omarchy 4.0.x also defaults to SDDM autologin rather than a conventional multi-user login flow. If you need a shared workstation before 4.1, expect to manage the display-manager and per-user configuration yourself.

See [Omarchy autologin and requiring a password after boot](autologin-and-password.qmd) before changing the login flow.
